line: Keep your boots out of the puddle, stranger.
Another cart robbed past Alder Bridge last night.
Dry salt pork, good rope—coin up front!
No credit for sellswords heading toward the fen.
Keep steel sheathed inside the market palisade.
Bridge toll's doubled since the northern watch vanished.
Bet you won't walk Lantern Passage after dark!
Mister, is that real blood on your scabbard?
Saw lights dancing in the peat—swear on ale!
Taxman drowned at the ford. Best spring ever.
Light a tallow stub before crossing the river.
Even the Sunken Sanctum remembers our forgotten prayers.
Don't step off the planks unless you fancy leeches.
My socks haven't been dry since last autumn.
Bog-moss poultices! Stops rot before it turns black!
Arrows cost extra when the causeway's flooded.
Check your boots for ticks before entering barracks.
Wardstone's humming louder again. Bad night ahead.
Found a shiny ring inside a dead frog!
Gran says hexers live under the willow roots.
Red mud stains forever—just like bad contracts.
Here's to the convoy! May it sink slowly.
Bless the dry ground, thin though it is.
Ashes cleanse what swamp water only rots.
Mind the curfew bell; wardens shoot first tonight.
Smoke from the harbor makes my eyes water.
Fine Oakhaven steel—guild-stamped and priced to hurt.
Scrolls fresh from the tower! Handle with dry hands.
State your company charter at the inner gate.
Keep clear of the Cinder Wards after sundown.
Look! A real mage with sparks in his beard!
My brother's on the harbor wall with a bow.
Guildmasters drink wine while we chew salt tack.
Sea's rising, Ember's marching—pour another cup!
May the old oaks stand against coming fire.
Tend the wounded; judgment waits at the gate.
Cough up the soot and keep moving, recruit.
Every forge in camp's been glowing three weeks straight.
Plate armor won't save fools, just dent prettier.
Buy your elixirs now—no shops past the ridge.
Malrik's name is mud here. Speak it softly.
Ash wind's blowing east—keep visors down.
I carry water buckets for the siege smiths!
Are you marching to the Court tomorrow?
Spent my last silver on steel instead of burial.
Ember wine burns twice going down!
Steel bends; only unbroken will crosses the ash.
Speak your regrets before the basalt road.
The river rose two notches overnight; tie the skiffs double.
Tax collectors wear heavier mail than the border militia now.
My brother went south to Redmarsh for timber wages. Haven't seen a copper.
Keep your hood up near the west gate; the wind cuts straight off the fens.
Move along, sellsword. Loitering near the granary gets you a night in irons.
Sheathe that steel inside the palisade, or I'll have it melted for horseshoes.
Two patrols went missing past Alder Bridge. Watch the reeds if you travel.
Papers in order? Good. Don't make me regret letting you through.
Smoked river-pike and pickled turnips—keeps for weeks in a wet saddlebag!
Lantern oil's doubled since the barges stopped running. Buy before dusk!
I don't buy blood-stained cloaks. Wash the mud off before you haggle.
Good hemp rope, tarred against rot—a lifesaver when the ford floods.
Mister, did you really kill a briar-hound? Can I see its teeth?
Ma says if I walk past the old mill at dusk, the creek-widow takes my shoes.
Bet I can skip a flat stone farther across the ford than you!
Saw eyes glowing in the willows last night... *hic*... swore it was a lantern...
Pour another turnip-gin! Tomorrow the Crown takes the rest of our barley anyway!
You look like a man who's seen a ghost... buy me a mug and I'll tell you mine.
Light a tallow candle for the river-dead, traveler; the current forgets no one.
The chapel roof leaks, yet the poor still come for dry bread and quiet prayer.
May the Shepherd guide your boots away from the deep silt.
Blessings cost nothing, though a copper for the orphanage keeps the hearth lit.
River damp eats cheap iron alive. Bring your blade here for a proper oil-quench.
Half my charcoal goes to arrowheads for the watch; wait your turn at the anvil.
Need a dent hammered out of that breastplate? Half a silver, payable now.
Good bog-iron is hard to smelt clean, but it holds an edge better than royal tin.
Spare a crust for an old ferryman? My knees gave out after forty winters on the oar.
A copper for the blind, friend—I still hear which way the crows fly before a raid.
The mud takes everything eventually; share a coin while your pockets are heavy.
Gods bless your sword arm, stranger. Don't end up shivering on these steps like me.
Boil your drinking water twice unless you fancy rotting from the belly out.
They pulled another sunken cart from the peat bog this morning—still had bones in it.
Don't step off the plank-walks after dark; the marsh swallows a horse in ten breaths.
Peat smoke stings the eyes, but it's the only thing keeping the midges off our skin.
Keep to the raised boardwalks. I'm not hauling your drowned carcass out of the reeds.
We burn the dead at sundown here. Anything buried in Redmarsh crawls back up.
Check your boots for leeches before entering the barracks.
No fires outside the stone braziers—marsh gas ignites faster than dry straw.
Bitter-root salve and dried willow bark! Wards off the swamp-ague for three days!
Waxed leather boots, double-stitched! Keep the black rot off your toes!
I pay good silver for pristine toad-glands and intact mire-wisp lanterns.
Salt's worth more than gold in this damp hell. Buy a pouch before the fog rolls in.
Look what I found in the mud—a rusted buckle! Think a knight wore it?
Don't follow the green lights out past the dikes; they're hungry ghosts!
I caught three fat frogs by the sluice gate before the guard chased me off.
Bog-shine burns the throat, aye, *hic*, but it kills the worms in your gut!
The dead whisper under the floorboards when the rain stops... pass the jug...
Came here to drain the marsh ten years ago. Now the marsh is draining me.
Anoint your brow with ash before walking the fen; the mire-heretics prey on the unwary.
Even in this drowned wasteland, the Light flickers for those who keep faith.
Speak the names of the lost so the fog does not steal their memory.
We tend the fever-wards day and night; bring clean linen if you have any to spare.
Peat fires run cooler than oak coal, so don't rush me while I temper your steel.
Every blade I forge here comes greased in tallow; leave it dry and it'll rust by dawn.
Bring me salvage from the sunken ruins and I'll hammer you something worth carrying.
My bellows wheeze worse than an old man in this fog, yet the anvil still rings.
Lost my left foot to the bog-rot; spare a coin so I don't starve on these planks.
A dry blanket or a copper piece—either keeps the grave away one more night.
They promised land to anyone who cleared the fen. All I got was the shaking fever.
Have pity, traveler. The crows are already eyeing my boots.
Another wreck washed up below the cliffs; the corsairs picked it clean before dawn.
Salt wind gets into your lungs and never leaves. You cough brine till you die.
Ships used to anchor here ten deep. Now only smugglers dare the reefs.
Keep one hand on your purse near the docks; the galley-slavers recruit with clubs.
Curfew sounds at the second bell. Anyone on the piers after dark gets shot on sight.
We hold this rock against pirates and sea-beasts alike. Don't start trouble in camp.
Check your powder horns—sea spray ruins a charge faster than rain.
Signal fires stay lit all night. If the beacon goes dark, draw your blade.
Hardtack, salted herring, and sour grog—proper rations for a rough crossing!
Salvaged brass, spyglasses, and waterproof oilskins! Fresh off the morning tide!
No haggling over whetstones; salt air dulls a sword edge in half a watch.
Need passage north? Pay the captain in silver, not promises.
I found a crab bigger than my head under the pier, and it snapped my stick in half!
Look at the big ship's ribs sticking out of the surf! Pa says ghosts sail it at night.
Bet you can't climb the sea-wall faster than me!
Fifteen years on a galley oar... *hic*... and I still feel the deck rocking under me...
Drink to the drowned lads! Better the cold sea than a corsair's lash!
I saw a barnacle-hulk crush a longboat like an egg... *hic*... pass the rum.
Cast a pinch of salt into the surf for those who never found harbor.
Beware the tide-priests along the coves; they worship hunger, not mercy.
The sea takes much, yet the stone chapel stands firm against every gale.
May steady winds and true steel see you safely through the Iron Coast.
I hammer anchor chains and harpoon heads all morning; your sword can wait till noon.
Sea-salt pits ordinary steel. Let me rub whale-oil into those joints for a copper.
Good heavy iron from the cliff-mines—shatters bone and barnacle shell alike.
Keep your shield boss tight; a corsair's boarding axe won't give you a second chance.
Washed ashore with nothing but the rags on my back; spare a coin for a survivor?
The cliffs took my ship and my crew. A crust of bread is all I ask now.
Cold wind off the bay cuts straight to the bone... help an old sailor out.
May the tide bring you fortune, stranger—and leave a copper in my bowl.
Ash falls like gray snow whenever the wind blows down from the Crownlands.
Half the noble houses are burning their own ledgers before the inquisitors arrive.
Keep your voice down in the square; the Ember Guard pays well for informants.
The great oaks beyond the wall are black skeletons now. Nothing green survives.
State your business in Oakhaven. No refugees allowed past the inner ward.
Keep your hands where I can see them. Tensions are high enough without armed fools.
The sky's been red for three nights straight. Stay behind the stone walls.
Any spark near the powder stores means the gallows. Extinguish your torches.
Fine wool cloaks and soot-masks! Breathe ash without one and you'll cough blood!
Last barrels of clean spring water from the hills! Price goes up at sundown!
Silver only today—royal script isn't worth the parchment it's printed on.
Fire-ward charms and cured leather! Best protection before you march on the Ember!
Why does the sky look like a giant fireplace, mister?
We sweep cinders off the porch every morning, and by supper it's gray again.
Pa hid our good silver under the hearthstone so the tax-knights won't find it.
To the Crown and Ember! *hic* May they both burn down to cold clinkers!
Wine tastes like soot lately... still washes the fear down...
I used to own three orchards outside town... *hic*... now I own this empty cup.
Pray for rain, traveler—not for crops, but to cool the madness in the capital.
Pride built the Cinder Crown, and pride shall reduce it to dust.
Step inside the sanctuary and wash the soot from your face; all are welcome here.
Hold fast to mercy when you face the pyre-knights; hate only feeds their fire.
I've forged steel for forty years, and I've never tempered blades for a darker road.
Bring me high-carbon ore; soft iron bends like tallow against royal plate.
My forge is hot enough already without the ash-wind blowing through the shutters.
A sharp edge and a stout shield—that's the only politics that matters now.
Our village burned three weeks ago; spare a copper so my children can eat tonight.
Even the lords will be begging in the ashes soon enough... help an old soul out.
Cinders in my lungs and nothing in my belly—have mercy, good warrior.
A coin for a prayer? I still remember the old hymns before the smoke came.
